text.text_excerpt: I've been to a fair amount of gay bars, and there are some that are welcoming of all people, and there are some that are not as much. Thankfully, this one is a welcoming bar. Everyone is really nice and friendly. Its not scene-y at all. It has a very relaxed atmosphere where I know I can get a drink with a few friends and have a good calm time. The bartender is really nice about changing the tv's to what ever you (or most people) want to watch. They do something special with every Saints game, but I forgot what is is. I stuck to beer that night, so I have no idea how the pour is on the cocktails, but the beer was decently priced. They charged my card to debit, so I don't know if they take...

My first time to The PAGE was awesome! It will definitely go down as my top pick Gay bar in New Orleans the next time that I visit. My friends and I were exploring different things on Bourbon street prior to our visit and found the "gay section" of the street really didn't offer much and the vibe was just off per say.. Now I know a great gay bar/club when I see one thanks to living in Atlanta, GA for a few years. Hard to compare actually but what I will say is that this is as good as it gets! When walking in you will notice that they do charge a $5 cover but it's absolutely worth it! CASH ONLY as most of the places are down in this area of town so be prepared on that piece of things. I agree with reviewer Vicky, this is a welcoming bar. For the most part, the clientele is nice, friendly and chatty. The bartender was really cool, struck up a decent conversation, and was some nice eye candy. I as well stuck to beer so I cannot comment on the pour of the drinks, but the Corona that I had was cold and relatively inexpensive. And yes, at the time I went there is no sign outside, but it is directly on the corner of Rampart and Toulouse.
